A second bird came up to dance
He danced his dance, he tried his best
But the first little bird was not impressed
She told him that his dance was swell
And bid him farewell.
Two little birds sitting on the fence
A third bird came right up to dance
He danced a little bit better than the last
But the first bird thought that it lacked class
She lied and said his dance was swell
And bid him farewell.
Three little birds sitting on the fence
A fourth bird came right up to dance
He danced a little bit better than the rest
But the first bird was still not impressed
She told him that his dance was swell
And bid him farewell.
Four little birds sitting on the fence
A fourth bird came right up to dance

And the first little bird was quite impressed
She told him that his dance was swell

It's been one month since the incident
When a shadow, tall and lean
Entered my house in a rainstorm
Teleporting, thus unseen.

It was content to stay awhile
Rummaging through the room
Touching all of its

contents
Slowly spelling out our doom.

'Twas not by mere coincidence
That later in the night
A burning log pulled from the hearth
Cast my abode alight.

With my house the inferno took
My dear and loving

wife;
Only I, burnéd and bruised
Could escape with my life.

And here I still stay, my world destroyed,
Cast in internal strife,
Waiting, watching for that shadow

book.foxcraft_dungeon_loot.fireblood.pag:
The screams in the next room grew louder.

Luna resisted the urge to shield her ears; the way that her hands were burning now, she'd probably just injure herself. Besides, the doctors had responded quickly. Frederic would be fine.

Unexpectedly, the screams subsided, replaced by whimpers, and Luna could hear a muttered curse. The door burst open and several technicians and the doctor excitedly rushed through. The head nurse quickly pulled the door shut, slamming the heavy bolt above the handle

into place. As he turned around, Luna could see the terror on his face, mingling with more than a hint of sadness. She noticed the expression on all of the other nurses' faces too, and one was clearly breaking down, sobbing silently in his coworker's comforting embrace.

Confused, Luna spoke. "Frederic... he... he's going to be fine, right?" She refused to believe otherwise if she didn't hear it from the nurses themselves.

"I'm sorry, miss," the doctor started, but as she turned to face Luna, she did not continue. Instead, her

eyes lingered on Luna's singed acolyte robes. The twinge of discomfort on her face. Her burning, reddened hands...

"SHIT," she cussed, "Somebody get her out of here! She doesn't need to see-"

%1$s

Fireblood. They were certain of it.

Luna's attending nurse Tamelise had somberly explained her predicament after leading her to the quarantine wards. Frederic had apparently been exposed, and was in the late stage if the illness when she

found him writhing in pain in the Arcaneum. The act of bringing him to the hospital, while noble, had allowed the living flame to make its way from Frederic to her. "We're so sorry," Tamelise said, "but there's nothing we can do... Fireblood has no known cure. All we can do is make you

comfortable in your final hours."

Making her "comfortable" was apparently limited to a menthol ointment and a morphine drip. Luna could barely think with the painkiller's heavy fog weighing on her consciousness. "...No known cure?" she mumbled. %1$s

%1$s

"I'm afraid not," confirmed Nurse Tamelise.

Luna felt numb, but not from the drip. %2$s she thought to herself. %3$s Even in her fogged-up state, the
Three years of being an Acolyte, and for what?
irony was not lost on her. %1$s Tears began to stream from her eyes as the grief began to push through the numbness. %2$s
Total control over fire, only to go up in flames. Poetic.
I can't save myself... I couldn't save Frederic...

book.foxcraft_dungeon_loot.lost_focus.pa:
%1$s

  "Kylie? Are you listening?"

  Kylie, who had been lost in thought, snapped to attention and winced. This was the third time this month she had been daydreaming during an important meeting, and definitely not the first

time her manager had to snap her focus back. "Y-yes, Harry, thank you," she replied sheepishly, "What... What were you saying again?"

  Harry sighed as he put his hand to his face. Not a good sign. Clearly she and him were going to have a chat about it after

the meeting. It definitely wasn't the first time they would have that chat either. "As I was saying..."

  Kylie tried to fix her attention to whatever Harry was droning on about but it kept slipping away like sand through her fingers. Her mind was often elsewhere, but her

grandfather's passing had made focusing on anything for more than a few hours much more difficult than she had even thought possible. She'd found herself thinking back to her childhood with him several times this past week alone.

  She noticed Harry

was looking directly at her again, and she realized that she'd let her focus slip yet again. Giving a start she frantically tried to catch up with her notes, feeling her face grow red until Harry looked away.

  Harry sighed again as he stood up. The rest of the team had

shuffled off to lunch, but Kylie stayed behind.

  "Uh, Harry. I'm..." she started, but the words caught in her throat.

  Harry held up a hand to stop her anyways. "It's okay, Kylie. I get it." He arranged the various timetables and

project design documents into a neat pile before slipping them into his slim loose-leaf binder and snapping the rings shut. "Losing a grandparent can be difficult; I know that."

  Kylie didn't say anything in return, averting her eyes from the plump man.

After a poignant pause, Harry continued. "How about you take the rest of the day off?" he suggested. "It's Friday, so I'm sure the team will manage."

  Kylie's embarrassment flared. "I- no, that's not necessary!" she insisted, though, to be

honest, it was an extremely tempting offer. "I'm fine, really. I'm fine."

  Maybe if she said it enough she could convince herself, but Harry wasn't falling for it. He slid the trapper-keeper over the conference table. "Here, review these when you can. Peter

can help give you any context you need, since you didn't seem to get much from this meeting. Take your time. I'll see you Monday."

  Harry left the room, and Kylie was left sitting in silence. She should have been grateful of Harry's understanding, and

willingness to accommodate, she figured. So why did she feel so much worse?

  Kylie didn't even stop for lunch on the way home. Instead, she took a meandering path back on the city bus lines. The train would have been quicker, and more
direct, but Kylie didn't want quick or direct. Not right now, when going home felt more like punishment than a relief.

%1$s


%2$s Time Immemorial, the God of the Sun MYSTERIA fought the DÆMON LORD MELIMONAS and sealed It away, deep below the Earth.

For a long time,
Chaptre I: Night
In

Humanity prospered under MYSTERIA's Light, building great civilizations and filling many libraries with the tales of their exploits.

But in their endless search for knowledge, they discovered the

prison of the DÆMON LORD, and loosed It upon the unsuspecting Earth once more.

Wasting no time, MELIMONAS struck out against MYSTERIA and, catching Them unawares, drove Them from the Sky. The DÆMON,

victorious, took the Earth as Its trophy, swallowing the entire world and blackening the Sky with an endless Night.

Generations passed, and Humanity dwindled. The forces of
MELIMONAS were relentless in their campaign against all that was blessed with MYSTERIA's Light. Cities fell. Libraries burned. Too much, lost to the Fires of MELIMONAS.

%1$s


%2$sut all was not lost.

When Humanity was at its lowest, a Hero was chosen by MYSTERIA Themself. She was a Knight, and her name was
Chaptre II: Knight
B

PALOMINA.

MYSTERIA appeared before PALOMINA, diminished, but still brilliant in Their Glory. And MYSTERIA spake unto PALOMINA,
"Harken well, Child, for Humanity is not yet lost. Thou art

their Final Hope."

And MYSTERIA bestowed upon PALOMINA a Gift, a Spear infused with Their own Light.

And MYSTERIA instructed, "Thou must take Mine Light to the highest point and

loose it upon the darkened Sky.

"Should its aim be true, and its bearer pure of heart, it shall strike down the DÆMON LORD and drive It from this place."

Thus spake MYSTERIA.

%1$s


%2$snd so PALOMINA set out towards the tallest peak, steadfast in her duty.

But MELIMONAS sensed MYSTERIA's Light and set upon PALOMINA
Chaptre III: Merchant
A

with Its forces. Wave after wave of enemies drained PALOMINA of her strength. And just when PALOMINA felt she could continue no longer, she met the Merchant.

But this was no ordinary Merchant. It was

none other than the DÆMON LORD Itself, disguised as a mere traveler.

"Ho, Knight," called MELIMONAS to the beleaguered PALOMINA, "you seem troubled, friend. Perhaps I may provide something to ease

your passage?"

And MELIMONAS presented her with a second Spear, infused with hidden Dark Intent.

"This shall aid your quest, of that, I am certain!"

Thus spake MELIMONAS.

PALOMINA, being none the wiser, accepted the gift, and bade the Merchant farewell. The forces of MELIMONAS thinned as PALOMINA's travel continued, and

though she thought it because of her newfound strength, it was simply that MELIMONAS knew It had already won.

Upon reaching the highest peak, PALOMINA called out, "MELIMONAS!

"I have beaten back Your forces! I have reached this, the highest peak in all the land, and I shall do battle unto You!"

Thus spake PALOMINA.

%1$s


%2$sELIMONAS simply laughed.

"Thou seek'st to do battle unto Me? Fine then, Knight. Level thy Spear at Me, and We shall see who is victorious."
Chaptre IV: Deception
M

Thus spake MELIMONAS.

But when PALOMINA took MYSTERIA's Spear, and heft it above her head to loose it, it shattered as glass in her hands.

For MELIMONAS was clever. It

knew MYSTERIA would not let any of Its dark forces wield the Spear. So little by little, bit by bit, its tainted Spear had corrupted PALOMINA, making her appear as one of the DÆMON LORD's own.

MELIMONAS

erupted into raucous laughter as the mortified PALOMINA scrambled to pick up the scattered Shards. "See now how thou hold'st no power over Me! But thou hast another Spear, dost thou not? Perhaps it shall be more

effective!"

Thus spake MELIMONAS.

PALOMINA, out of options, and not knowing the Dark Spear's blighted provenance, heft the Dark Spear above her head. But when she tried to loose the
Spear, it held onto her with tendrils of oozing Darkness and pulled her high into the Sky.

%1$s


%2$soolish little insect!" exclaimed the DÆMON LORD, "Thou didst think to best Me?

"Now thou art Mine, suspended in Mine Night! Now thou must watch as thy
Chaptre V: Loss
"F

precious Humanity burns, along with the rest of MYSTERIA's wretched Light!"

Thus spake MELIMONAS.

And MELIMONAS besieged PALOMINA's mind with horrors.

Towns abandoned. Children orphaned. Plague rampant. Famine ascendant. Death omnipresent.

The fall of Humanity itself.

PALOMINA struggled against the tide of omens as they
threatened to pull her under, deep into a sea of her own despair.

%1$s


%2$sarken!" The voice of MYSTERIA whispered from the Shards of Light, "Fear not, Child, for Humanity is not yet lost.

"Thou art their
Chaptre VI: Light
"H

final hope, and thou must take what remains of Mine Light, and loose it upon the Sky. It shall strike the DÆMON LORD as a thousand piercing bolts, and We shall drive It from this place."

Thus spake

MYSTERIA.

Slowly, PALOMINA understood. She needed not a Spear, but the Light, and the DÆMON LORD was much closer than before.

%1$s


%2$sÆMON!" PALOMINA exclaimed, her resolve returning. "If You seek Our destruction, then I must not waver!"

Thus spake
Chaptre VII: Resolve
"D

PALOMINA.

And with a mighty throw, she loosed the thousands of Shards from her grasp.

MELIMONAS screamed, as MYSTERIA's searing Light tore through Its

Night, dotting its surface with a thousand-thou-
sand bright, shimmering stars. As MYSTERIA's Light poured through, PALOMINA brandished the DÆMON LORD's own Dark Spear, the Shadow was rent from the Spear by

the Glory of MYSTERIA's Light.

PALOMINA took aim at the DÆMON LORD, and once again loosed herself upon It, tearing a shimmering hole straight through MELIMONAS and Its Night. It was large enough to

dwarf all others but the Sun itself.

But even cleansed the Dark Spear refused to release PALOMINA's hand. And thus did it carry PALOMINA far beyond the Sky, and deep into the Night she

pierced.

PALOMINA would never again return to the Earth, but she left behind the wound rent through the DÆMON's Night; a brilliant Moon to mark her sacrifice.

%1$s


%2$sever again was MELIMONAS' Night so Dark that MYSTERIA could not banish it from the Sky.

And as a new dawn rose upon Humanity, they
Chaptre Final: Apotheosis
N

all sang the name of their Hero:

"PALOMINA! Wielder of the Spears of Light and Dark! The Goddess of the Moon!

"May she ever return to us in Glory, and in Light!"
Thus spake Humanity, and thus was PALOMINA ascendant.

book.foxcraft_dungeon_loot.the_endless_w:
%1$s

  Liara Thimbleweed was always obsessed with her dreams. She catalogued each one upon waking, and studied her notes and ramblings for common threads and misbegotten omens, hoping that one day she would find something useful, or
Chapter I

insightful, or prophetic. She'd actually managed to save a village from a flood once that way, though not even she was sure whether that was fate or simply coincidence. Lately though...

  "...I open my eyes, and it's like I haven't. I can't see my hand in

front of my face. The air is damp, and cold as ice. It freezes in my chest, burns on every breath. The ground is... wet, or icy. I don't dare move lest I fall.

  "There's a dreadful silence. It's louder than any silence ought to be. I call out, but my voice feels

muffled, as though the air itself abhors the sound. For a time, all I hear is the quickening pace of my own heart.

  "But it's interrupted by a new sound: like a hammer striking an anvil. It's far away, but I creep towards it, each footfall threatening to dash me against the ice.

Soon, I hear voices. They're guttural, and aren't speaking any language I can understand. The din begins to lift as I get closer, and soon, I see torchlight shining through a crack, the small beam reflecting off the frozen cave walls in a sparkling glory.

"You'd think I would think better of it, but something almost compels me to peer through the crack. I hunch down and stare through the small portal. My eyes scream from the sudden brightness, but I don't blink... can't blink. Because looking through the hole, I see Drauven. Dozens

of them. Wrapped in thick furs, huddling around makeshift braziers, striking the rock with stolen pickaxes, almost feverish in their search for... something. Me?

  "I scramble to get up, but slip on the frozen floor. I scream as skin tears

against the sharp rocks and blood splashes against the ice. The pickaxes stop, and the light from the crack suddenly dims...

  "They've found me.

  "My arm is broken from the fall. Cold and adrenaline dim the pain as I scrabble to right myself. A loud

roar is followed by the din of pickaxes against the thin wall separating me from them, but I am upright, and as I start to run down the slippery path I can hear the cave wall crumble behind me. My ears are full of frantic Drauven speech as they pour into my thin tunnel. In my terror, I

look back, but I lose my footing. The floor rushes to meet me as I let out a scream..."

  "...And that's when you wake up, isn't it?" Timur interjected.

  Liara stared into the depths of the fire. The rolling coals glowed brightly as the flames licked happily

at fresh logs, but Liara pulled her cloak tighter, as though staving off the memory of the cold. "Yeah," she finally replied. "That's when I wake up."

  Timur poked at the fire with his pike, sending fluttering sparks skyward. He remembered the look

in her eyes when he rushed to her side as she screamed herself awake. It was the fourth time in a week that had happened.

  "I know what you're thinking... maybe it's nothing. Maybe I'm... overreacting." Liara sighed, loosening her grip on her cloak. "Just Liara being

weird about her dreams again. But there's something here. I can't just ignore this. You understand that, right?"

  Timur was silent for a beat as he pushed a log further into the fire. He wasn't one to put such importance in dreams, but it was

clear enough to him that this whole ordeal was eating away at Liara. He could tell her it was just a dream; that she was safe, that she could ignore it, that she had to let it go or she'd keep having it; keep waking up in a cold sweat, screaming...

  Instead, he sighed.
"Okay," he said. "Where are we headed?"

%1$s

  "This is it," Liara said. She didn't know how she knew this was the cave from her dream, but she was certain it was.

  Timur wasn't so easily convinced, however. "How could you possibly know that? It looks the
Chapter II

same as every other cave we went by!"

  The two had been traveling for weeks now. The morning following Liara's dream, they bade their friends farewell and set off towards Greenhaven on a hunch. Timur flinched internally just thinking of the

impracticality of it all. But Liara was convinced: if they head towards Greenhaven, she was certain they'd find the cave. Timur remained skeptical.

  "I just don't see how this cave is any different from the last three we looked at." Timur grunted and

shifted the weight of his pack on his shoulders. "Though I suppose if it's not crawling with Deepists, it'll be an improvement."

  Liara was too busy unpacking her gear to respond. Besides, Timur knew what he was getting into when he agreed to join her

on this mission. "Leave that," she instructed as Timur readjusted his pack once more. "It'll only slow us down, and besides, if it's anything like my dream there won't be much room for maneuvering a large pack about anyways."

  Timur set the pack down, half

begrudgingly, half relieved to be free of its burden. He unsheathed a pickaxe from its side and holstered it against his belt as Liara produced a willow-hewn bow from her own pack. "You sure about that? I doubt there's gonna be much room to shoot in a cave."
"She's old reliable," quipped Liara, "but a dagger might also be... prudent." Timur grunted again before heading into the cave, and Liara followed close behind.

%1$s

  The room was small, and warmly lit by recessed ceiling fixtures. Along one of the white walls an oak bookshelf stood, housing several slim electronic reading devices. A large tan and brown clay pot sat in a corner opposite the shelves,

housing a lush green exotic fern, and on the back wall, a window stood half open, a cool, spring breeze entering the room. In the center of the room sat a large, black desk. On either side of the desk, two men sat in velvet colored chairs. The one on the side closest to the front

of the room was dressed in a formal black suit with a red tie. His blond-brown hair was combed to the side, and his blue-green eyes stared out through rectangular spectacles resting on his slender nose. He seemed young, in his late twenties, at most. If this man could be

considered a young professional, with his slight figure and sharp suit, the man that sat across from him could be considered the absolute antithesis. His thinning, greying black hair was uncombed, but not messy. With his age placed around fifty, he was much pudgier

than the other, and wore a short sleeved, white dress shirt. The black tie around his neck hung loosely. His brown eyes were directed at a sheet of paper on the desk. The younger man fidgeted in his seat as the latter continued to read.

  Finally the older man

straightened up, adjusted his tie, and spoke. "Your résumé checks out well," he said in a gruff tone. "I'm just gonna have to run a thorough background check; nothing personal, just company policy." The younger man nodded, twiddling his thumbs.

  The older man

tapped the surface of his desk, which immediately woke like a computer from a screensaver. Upon its surface, a keyboard appeared, as well as a clock. A glass pane extended from the desk, upon which was projected the company logo: a stylized waterfowl with outstretched wings

and its beak pointed into the sky. The man pressed a quick series of keys. The computer-desk dinged a confirmation tone, and a window appeared on the glass pane. The window displayed a picture of the younger man, along with several lines of text. The older man

quickly scanned the text, nodded slightly, and closed the window.

  "You're clean," said the interviewer after a short pause. "The computer'll gauge your potential, and we'll get back to you in a couple of months. Thanks for your time, Mr. Tyler. We look forward to your

working here." The interviewer half-stood and extended a hairy arm. Mr. Tyler got up and shook the hand firmly. Nodding slowly, the interviewer sat down one more, and Mr. Tyler, taking the cue to leave, turned and left, the automatic doors closing behind him with a soft hiss.
book.foxcraft_dungeon_loot.the_new_war.p:
%1$s

  So... we're fighting them, they're fighting us. Neither of us refuses to cede even an inch. Our greatest military minds hatch a plan: they give up. Not entirely, mind you: they set up a DMZ. A huge wall and an

area of land so treacherous neither us nor them can get through it without suffering major casualties. And they sit their asses down and wait. The idea is, eventually the aliens will get so complacent that humanity will be

able to just spin back up its war efforts and wipe them out in a couple of generations.

  Couple generations pass, about a hundred years. Humanity has, by and large, not even seen an alien in that time,

but %1$s been lying in wait, training for the moment that we strike back. Our AIs and databanks keeping the strategic knowledge alive. Right?

  %2$s, WRONG! Turns out the aliens we left our walls to fight are

the same damn aliens our forebears fought, down to the individual! And they haven't lost a step. Whatever they endured on the long trip here, combined with three hundred years of fighting us? A million times more effective a

teacher than sims and drills could ever be. Our greatest military minds put their heads together and not a one thought "Wait, what if these things don't age like us?" and now WE'RE the complacent ones losing steps in a

war that used to be a stalemate.

  No ifs, ands, or buts about it, we are Fucked. Capital-F Fucked. They haven't invented a state of being Fucked that's Fucked as much as we are Fucked right now.
Well, I've had enough. I'm not wasting my life fighting these immortal fucking spiders any longer! Next cargo ship home I'm taking it, I swear!
